top.title: ‘Absolutely despicable’: Former teammate rips Aaron Rodgers for ‘unnecessary’ Mike McCarthy comments
top.description: Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images The Pittsburgh Steelers epitomized organizational dysfunction on Wednesday night. After the team announced late on Tuesday night that veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers wouldn’t be starting Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos and would be inactive instead, Rodgers decided to call into The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday afternoon. During his call, Rodgers asserted that Steelers head coach MikeMcCarthy had completely checked out and was falling asleep and snoring in team meetings and had lost most of the locker room when he ended a rambling speech in the locker room with “One, two, three, Packers!” On a potential return to the organization, Rodgers said “that ship has sailed,” and sure enough, the four-time NFL MVP was released later that day. Despite multiple sports media members and former Steelers saying their sources within the organization had confirmed Rodgers’ claims, one of Rodgers’ former teammates, T.J. Lang, who played with the quarterback with the Green Bay Packers under McCarthy, was disgusted with Rodgers’ tell-all. “I think it’s despicable,” Lang said on 97.1 The Ticket. “I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has bitched about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates, airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media. He has blacklisted, I don’t know how many, former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he was sick of it. Honestly, I don’t even know if I want to watch the whole thing. It’s just unnecessary. “It’s a victim mentality. It’s a poor me, woe is me. Oh, I thought this, and it wasn’t that. And I’m sick, man. I’ve been in a group chat with, with a whole lot of former teammates that feel the exact same way that I do.” Lang went on to say that Rodgers’ behavior was completely unnecessary and that in his eight years playing under McCarthy, he came away loving the coach. TJ Lang on his former teammate Aaron Rodgers https://t.co/0oiS3PybCn — 97.1 The Ticket: (@971theticketxyt) November 25, 2026 “And I talked to Mike McCarthy on Monday night, and, still have a great relationship with him. I haven’t talked to Aaron Rodgers in probably five years. I can’t remember the last time he returned a text. I don’t have a relationship with him. And I think it’s just absolutely despicable what he just did to Big Mike. “Truth or not, truth or not, nobody knows. We’re not in those meetings. We don’t know that. But to air the grievances and to completely try to bury a man that you’ve been a quarterback under for going back to Green Bay, I don’t know, 15, 16 seasons?” It’ll be interesting to see if and how this impacts Rodgers’ legacy. Whatever the case, if this is it for the quarterback, who has been steadfast throughout the season that this would be his final one in the NFL and reportedly doesn’t have a ton of interest at the moment, it’s an ugly end to what’s been a spectacular career. top.title: Tigers agree with Kevin Gausman, workhorse pitcher, on 1-year contract
top.description: Scott Harris was not joking about adding pitching this offseason. The Detroit Tigers are in agreement with right-hander Kevin Gausman , first reported Wednesday, Nov. 25, by ESPN . Gausman is reportedly set to sign a one-year, $25 million contact, pending a physical. He went 9-12 in 2026 with a 4.52 ERA, 1.27 WHIP and 184 strikeouts between the Chicago Cubs and Toronto Blue Jays . Gausman will be 36 years old in January. He was the No. 4 overall pick in the 2012 MLB Draft out of LSU. He is from Baton Rouge. On Tuesday, the Tigers extended right-hander Troy Melton to a lucrative, six-year contract . They signed two pitchers earlier in free agency, reliever Emilio Pagán and 2024 American Rookie of the Year starter Luis Gil . They also signed infielder Ha-Seong Kim on Tuesday. Gausman joins a Tigers projected starting rotation of Melton, Framber Valdez and Jackson Jobe. They also have Keider Montero, Drew Anderson and River Ryan; Ryan, 28, was acquired in the Tarik Skubal trade. top.title: Steelers’ Nick Herbig still limited ahead of Broncos game
top.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images With Aaron Rodgers’ televising his exposé on the Steelers and eventually being released Wednesday, it’s easy to forget that Pittsburgh still held a team practice ahead of a Black Friday matchup with the Denver Broncos. In the Steelers’ Wednesday injury report, outside linebacker Nick Herbig remained limited in practice for the second straight day as he recovers from a hip/ribs injury that caused him to miss Pittsburgh’s Week 11 game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Notably, the Steelers had several new names join the availability report, with safety DeShon Elliott (knee) and linebacker Cole Holcomb (ankle) appearing as limited. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers, now off the team, was unsurprisingly a non-participant for “personal” reasons; veteran defender Cam Heyward was also given a rest day. Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith (ankle) and wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) did not participate for the second straight practice on Wednesday. Still in their 21-day return windows from injured reserve, wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie guard Gennings Dunker continued to log full practices. #Steelers Week 12 Wednesday Injury Report pic.twitter.com/YfbJJfw21s — Alan Saunders (@ASaunders_PGH) November 25, 2026 As for Denver, safety Taylor Rapp (limited; quadricep) and defensive end Sai’vion Jones (DNP; hamstring) were listed as out, but the rest of the team appears healthy. Running back Tyler Badie, who has logged full practices this week, is expected to be activated from IR at some point with the Broncos’ JK Dobbins serving a one-game team suspension this week. The Steelers have not yet released game designations for Black Friday’s game.

top.title: Tigers add another veteran on prove-it deal with MLB lockout looming
top.description: The Detroit Tigers are having an interesting offseason. The team has plenty of holes across the roster, but the front office is operating with a clear budget in mind. That is why they traded Tarik Skubal at the trade deadline earlier this year, because they knew they could not afford him. That has forced the team to take chances on players who are looking to prove they are worth more money long-term. MORE: Luis Gil leaves Yankees for American League rivals on $2.3 million contract They have already signed three players on prove-it deals, including shortstop Ha-Seong Kim on a one-year, $5 million deal, Emilio Pagan on a one-year, $11.5 million deal and Luis Gil on a one-year, $2.3 million contract. Pagan will take over as closer while Kim should get plenty of starts at shortstop. Gil should fight for an opportunity in the starting rotation. Detroit Tigers manager A.J. Hinch walks off the field after a pitching change against Minnesota Twins during the seventh inning at Comerica Park in Detroit on Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit is not done though. On Wednesday, the Tigers added another veteran, but not a bat or a relief arm. This time it is for the starting rotation. According to ESPN’s Jeff Passan, Detroit signed right-hander Kevin Gausman to a one-year, $25 million deal to bolster the rotation. The deal is pending a physical. As Passan mentions, Gausman has been a workhorse even though he is 35 years old. His on-field results trended downward in 2026, however. top.title: Motorcycle rider who took stunning cricket catch found
top.description: "I told my friend riding the motorcycle to duck his head. I'm going to catch it." These are the words of Mehran Khan, who amazed sports fans around the world when he caught a cricket ball while sitting on the back of a moving motorcycle. Mehran was passing a match in the Swat Premier League in Mingora when a ball sailed out of the ground towards him, with the passenger reaching out to catch it one-handed. Speaking to the BBC, he said of the grab, which has gone viral online: "I didn't think I would actually catch it." The employee of the Public Health Engineering Department was on his way home from work when he saw the ball being struck. "I'm a cricket fan. I play cricket myself and I watch it too. I saw that Abrar Lala was at the crease and then he hit a six," he said. "I told him [the friend who was driving] to duck his head. I'm going to catch it. Then I caught it." "I made the effort, but I didn't expect to catch it. I thought it would fall somewhere nearby, but by the grace of God I managed to catch it." According to Mehran, immediately after the catch the Swat Premier League organisers announced a prize of 10,000 Pakistani rupees (about £27.60) for him, funded by the Pakistan Army. The Marghazar resident was caught by surprise when the recording of the catch spread so quickly online, saying: "The video went viral overnight. I didn't even know about it." He expressed his happiness at receiving the award, saying he was grateful to God, and added that he had returned the ball after taking the catch. "People are saying I was taking the ball away with me, but that's not true. I returned it," he said. Swat Strikers won the match against GKR Dir by 34 runs, and Mehran urged the organisers to continue holding the tournament every year, describing it as an "excellent competition". Mehran Khan is from Marghazar in the Swat region of northern Pakistan [BBC] One of the most unusual catches There have been several remarkable catches by spectators at cricket matches in the past. In 1987, during a match in Australia, a cameraman casually caught one of former England all-rounder Ian Botham's sixes while holding a cigarette in his mouth. In 2014, during a New Zealand domestic match, a spectator slid down a slope and completed a one-handed catch. Last year, in a match between Australia and South Africa, a fan caught a ball with one hand while holding two drink cans in the other. Mehran's one-handed catch while sitting on a moving motorcycle will join them in cricketing history. Get cricket news sent straight to your phone

top.title: Trev Alberts' attorney plans to file lawsuit against Michigan
top.description: Lawyers for Trev Alberts, who had been hired by Michigan as its next athletic director before the university’s President-elect C. Cybele Raver and current Michigan President Domenico Grasso formally withdrew the university's offer of employment this week, are planning to file a lawsuit against the University of Michigan seeking millions in damages. Alberts’ attorney, Tom Mars, told The Detroit News on Wednesday, Nov. 25, the lawsuit could be filed in a “few weeks” either in Texas, where Alberts had been athletic director at Texas A&M before Michigan hired him, or in Michigan. Raver, who does not begin her tenure at Michigan until Dec. 1, hired Alberts and may also be included as a defendant in the case, Mars said. “It's just a straight up breach of contract,” said Mars, noted for high-profile college sports litigation, including coaching and administrative disputes. “They agreed to pay him $17.2 million plus $4 million, and then they changed their mind after they induced him to leave his job.” Mars said the memorandum of understanding is contractually binding and Michigan will have to pay the full contract, $17,205,352. The MOU had no reference to a background check that would prevent Alberts from being hired. Michigan also had agreed to pay Alberts’ $4 million buyout to Texas A&M. Alberts is now responsible to pay the buyout. “I want to put the whole case together and show Michigan what it looks like,” Mars said, “and then they can decide whether they want to spend the time and the energy defending it or not.” Alberts was hired by Michigan on Nov. 17 and signed a memorandum of understanding. He had not been formally announced as Michigan’s next athletic director replacing Warde Manuel, who planned to step down at the end of this year . Alberts was informed late Monday night, Nov. 23, he would no longer be the Michigan athletic director by a representative from the search firm ZRG Turnkey, which Michigan hired for its national search. Manuel, on Wednesday, agreed to remain at Michigan until an interim or permanent athletic director is hired. Michigan cited the results of a background check in its decision to rescind Alberts' hiring , saying the information gathered during the employment process provided "good cause" to end its agreement with him, according to a letter dated Tuesday, Nov. 24 sent to Alberts. The letter, signed by Grasso and Raver, formally withdrew the university's offer of employment and ended negotiations with Alberts "with good cause to terminate the MOU." The change of heart from Michigan comes amid scrutiny of Alberts' comments in an ongoing federal lawsuit, first reported by The Detroit News, that accuses University of Nebraska-Lincoln officials, including Alberts, of mishandling a sexual relationship between an associate women's basketball coach and a player during his tenure as the athletic director. top.title: Caleb Williams Wants to Give Someone Else the Thanksgiving He Remembers
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Before Caleb Williams became the Chicago Bears’ quarterback, Thanksgiving football meant a spot on the couch beside his dad. His mom made creamed spinach, they grabbed a bag of Tostitos, and the games became part of the holiday. It’s a familiar scene for football fans: food on the table, family in the room and the television on while the afternoon slips into evening. Williams remembers watching the Dallas Cowboys and another NFC team playing while he and his dad enjoyed the snack. On Thursday, he’ll be on the other side of the screen. Williams and the Bears visit the Detroit Lions in a Thanksgiving game with far more at stake than holiday bragging rights. Both teams enter 8-2, and the winner will leave Ford Field alone atop the NFC North. For Williams, the occasion is also a chance to give another family a memory like the ones he grew up with. “Now I get to be a part of making memories for somebody else,” he said during his Tuesday press conference . “We want to go out there and we want to put on a show and have fun doing it.” A familiar tradition, a bigger stage Nov 28, 2013; Detroit, MI, USA; Fox reporter Erin Andrews interviews Detroit Lions quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) after the game against the Green Bay Packers during a NFL football game on Thanksgiving at Ford Field. Detroit won 40-10. Mandatory Credit: Tim Fuller-USA TODAY Sports The Lions have been a fixture of Thanksgiving football for generations. For Williams, playing in the game he once watched at home is part of what makes the opportunity special. “As a kid, you were sitting at home watching this with your parents,” he added. “I was sitting at home watching these games with my pops, eating some food that my mom made.” Now, children who settle in with their own families could spend the afternoon watching Williams try to deliver a statement win. The quarterback knows the matchup brings plenty of excitement, and he said games like this are easier to get up for. Chicago has won five straight, while Detroit brings a six-game winning streak into Thursday. Both teams have the same record, but the Bears are still looking for their first NFC North victory after earlier losses to Minnesota and Green Bay. The last Bears-Lions Thanksgiving meeting also gives this trip a complicated place in Chicago’s recent history. In 2024, Williams and the Bears rallied from a 23-7 deficit, only for the game to end after a mismanaged final sequence left a timeout unused. Head coach Matt Eberflus was fired the following day. Two years later, Williams returns with a different head coach and a team playing for first place. Ben Johnson, who was Detroit’s offensive coordinator for that 2024 game, now leads Chicago into a matchup against his former team. top.title: Set point #14: A season in review
top.description: There’s no denying the fact that there was a lot of bad this season. Northwestern finished the year 8-20 overall and 1-16 in the Big Ten, losing 14 straight games before beating Iowa in the final week. The ‘Cats were swept 10 times during Big Ten play and ranked at the bottom of the conference in most of the major statistical categories, including wins. The season started off with a disappointing loss to a George Mason team that went .500 in its conference slate, and ended with a stretch of 16 losses in 17 games. There’s no other way to put it: the ‘Cats were not a good volleyball team. However, as I’ve spent the majority of the past 13 editions of this column critiquing the lack of competitiveness shown by Northwestern, I’ll try to keep the season finale one of hope. And, don’t get it twisted, there is hope to be had. Maya Stillwell and Hayley Schaaf broke out as a freshman middle duo. Stillwell ended the year with 120 kills and a team-high 82 blocks while hitting .279 in her 100 sets played. Schaaf totaled 86 kills and 35 blocks while hitting a team-high .299. The two steadily improved throughout the year, and Stillwell looked like one of the conference’s better middle blockers at times toward the end of the season. Both Stillwell and Schaaf can improve their blocking rhythm and attacking precision heading into next season, but if both stay with the ‘Cats, they should form a youthful and exciting middle group when combined with sophomore Kayla Kauffman. Setter Ellie Stiernagle was another impressive freshman. Though she had some defensive issues at points throughout the season, she became the staple of Northwestern. Stiernagle started 26 of the 26 matches she appeared in, finishing the year with 910 assists. She also had 16 aces and 46 blocks to go along with 188 digs. At 6-foot-2, Stiernagle is tall enough to play all around, and she proved it throughout the year. Northwestern’s serve receive was a big problem this season, but Stiernagle frequently gave her hitters chances to swing despite less-than-ideal passes. Sophomore libero Lauren Dignan was the major bright spot on the defensive end. She averaged 3.59 digs per set, good for seventh in the Big Ten, totaling 337. Although it was hard to defend with a questionable NU block often allowing clean hits or weird touches, Dignan did the best she could to cover the entire floor. Northwestern had three quality liberos on the roster, including Drew Wright and Gigi Navarrete, but Dignan was the one most trusted in the opposite-colored jersey. If the block can improve and the passing around her is shored up, Dignan could be in for a breakout junior season. The other key pieces of the team that will return next season are the two kill leaders, junior opposite hitter Mara Stiglic and sophomore outside hitter Bella Bullington. top.title: Mike McCarthy addresses Aaron Rodgers’ explosive criticism, confirms ’embarrassing’ Packers gaffe
top.description: Credit: Pittsburgh Steelers On Wednesday, now-former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers unloaded on coach Mike McCarthy after his demotion from the starting lineup. Afterward, McCarthy had a chance to respond. Late Tuesday night, the Steelers announced in a statement that Rodgers had been benched in favor of backup Mason Rudolph. Given the odd hour and the lack of explanation for the sudden change, speculation ran wild over what led to the decision. Rodgers got the chance to offer his side of the story on Wednesday with a visit to his old stomping grounds , The Pat McAfee Show . There, the four-time NFL MVP went off, accusing McCarthy of repeatedly falling asleep during team meetings, failing to make an effort to get to know the defensive players, and broadly suggesting the Steelers’ head coach is struggling to keep up with the rigors of coaching an NFL team. Rodgers also spilled some embarrassing details about McCarthy, including “snoring” during meetings and ending a halftime speech against the Eagles by saying “one, two, three, Packers.” The Steelers released Rodgers following the appearance. Later on Wednesday, McCarthy met with the media as Pittsburgh prepares to play the Broncos on Friday. top.title: An Unexpected Name Leads the Timberwolves in Net Rating
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trey Lyles doesn’t need to score 20 points to leave a mark on a game. On Monday, nine points were enough for his impact to stand out in the box score if you looked all the way to the last column. The Minnesota Timberwolves outscored the Brooklyn Nets by 29 points during Lyles’ 24 minutes in their 142-116 victory. It was another productive night for a reserve who has become one of the most reliable pieces of Chris Finch’s rotation. That performance also helped sustain one of the more surprising numbers on Minnesota’s roster. Through 18 games, Lyles leads the Timberwolves’ regular rotation players with a plus-13.7 net rating , according to NBA.com . In other words, Minnesota has outscored opponents by 13.7 points per 100 possessions with him on the floor. There are two names above him on the full team list. Anthony Edwards has a plus-23.1 rating in four games before his knee surgery, while Johni Broome’s plus-70.0 comes from just 2.5 minutes in one appearance. Among the players Finch has regularly relied on, Lyles sits just ahead of Jaden McDaniels at plus-13.4 and LaMelo Ball at plus-13.3. A net rating doesn’t capture an individual player’s value on its own. It reflects what happens with all five players on the floor and can be influenced by lineups, opponents and a relatively small early-season sample. Still, for a veteran whose contributions don’t always command attention, the number offers a reason to look more closely. Lyles knows what to look for Nov 4, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Houston Rockets forward Tari Eason (17) shoots against Minnesota Timberwolves forward Trey Lyles (41) in the second half at Toyota Center. Mandatory Credit: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images Lyles has a name for the kind of work that helps explain why his teams can thrive during his minutes: winning plays. Sometimes they show up clearly. A rebound ends an opponent’s possession. A blocked shot prevents a basket. A pass creates an open look for a teammate. Other times, the contribution is harder to find in the stat sheet. Lyles might box out so someone else can collect the rebound, close a gap before a driver gets there or make the pass that leads to an assist. “Just like the little intangibles and the things that might not show up in the stat sheet, but if you’re actually watching the game, you’re like, ‘Oh, OK, that guy’s doing something to help the team win,’” Lyles told Michael Rand of the Minnesota Star Tribune . He listed loose balls, rebounding, helping defensively and making an extra pass among the examples. They aren’t glamorous responsibilities, but they are the sort of details Minnesota has needed while navigating injuries and integrating several new players. Lyles told Rand that the work is recognized inside the locker room. Teammates notice when someone fills a gap or makes the extra effort, even if the play doesn’t produce a highlight. Devakumar Edwin, vice-president of oil and gas at Dangote Group, announced the development on Wednesday, according to a Reuters report. The listing comes after the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved the refinery’s share allocation plan following its heavily oversubscribed IPO, which closed last month. The regulatory approval cleared the way for the company to distribute shares to investors and proceed with preparations for its stock market debut. The refinery had earlier sought to increase the size of its IPO by up to 30 per cent to approximately $2.1 billion following strong investor demand. On September 11, Aliko Dangote, president of Dangote Industries Limited (DIL), said the refinery planned to pursue a listing on a United States stock exchange after expanding its production capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day within the next two and a half years. However, on November 8, Dangote disclosed that the refinery’s IPO fell short of its target of attracting 10 million investors. Despite missing the target, Africa’s richest person said the offer attracted “millions of investors”. nigeria.title: Nigeria Joins Global Pact To Protect Marine Biodiversity, Unlock Ocean Resources
nigeria.description: Nigeria has secured a significant international milestone for the country’s marine and blue economy, following its formal ratification of a landmark United Nations treaty on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. The historic instrument of ratification was deposited on behalf of President Bola Tinubu by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. ﻿ Speaking at the ceremony, Ibrahim highlighted the economic and strategic importance of the agreement to Nigeria, noting that it would expand the country’s opportunities to benefit from ocean resources through greater participation in the governance of the high seas. The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty, provides a framework for the protection, management and sustainable use of marine resources in areas beyond national jurisdiction. For Nigeria, a coastal nation along the Gulf of Guinea, the agreement marks a significant step towards strengthening its marine economy, protecting biodiversity, supporting fisheries and unlocking opportunities in emerging ocean-based industries. A major implication of the ratification is Nigeria’s plan to develop a proposal for the establishment of a highly protected marine area on the high seas. The initiative is also expected to strengthen efforts to conserve marine ecosystems while promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits from ocean resources, particularly for developing countries. Nigeria signed the BBNJ Agreement on May 3, 2024. Following the deposit of its instrument of ratification, the agreement will enter into force for Nigeria on December 24, 2026. This will enable the country to participate as a full Party at the first Conference of the Parties, scheduled to open on January 11, 2027. At the ceremony, Ibrahim acknowledged Evelyn Campos Sanchez, Officer-in-Charge of the United Nations Treaty Section, for receiving Nigeria’s instrument of ratification. Nigeria’s commitment to the agreement is further reinforced by the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, alongside the adoption of a National Blue Economy Policy and a national roadmap for implementing the treaty. nigeria.title: 4 African countries to have produced Miss Universe winners
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African contestants have earned the Miss Universe crown six times, across four countries. South Africa leads with three wins, while Namibia, Botswana and Angola have each won once. The titleholders claimed their crowns between 1978 and 2019, giving each country a place in the pageant’s history. The latest milestone achieved by an African nation is from Miss Universe 2024 where Nigeria’s Chidimma Adetshina finished as first runner-up and was named Miss Universe Africa and Oceania. That was a notable result for Nigeria, but it did not add another country to the list of African Miss Universe winners as the overall crown went to Denmark’s Victoria Kjær Theilvig. Here are the four African countries ranked by the number of Miss Universe crowns their representatives have won. South Africa: three wins South Africa has won the title three times. Margaret Gardiner became the country’s first winner in 1978. Demi-Leigh Nel-Peters won in 2017, and Zozibini Tunzi followed in 2019. Tunzi was the third South African winner and the first Black South African woman to earn the crown. Namibia: one win Michelle McLean won Miss Universe in 1992, becoming the first and, according to the pageant’s official profile, so far the only Namibian woman to win. The win came two years after Namibia gained independence in 1990. Botswana: one win Mpule Kwelagobe won the title in 1999. She remains the only woman from Botswana to be crowned Miss Universe, according to the pageant’s official legacy page. Angola: one win Leila Lopes won Miss Universe in 2011, becoming the first Angolan titleholder. The official Miss Universe legacy page records her win and notes that she later served as national director of Miss Angola Universe. nigeria.title: Gordon hits brace as Barcelona cruise to 4-1 Sabah win
nigeria.description: Anthony Gordon struck twice as Barcelona eased to a 4-1 victory at Sabah in the Champions League to boost their chances of a top eight league phase finish. The Catalan giants were without teenage star Lamine Yamal for the long journey east, but found their rhythm after a slow start to claim the three points and a fourth win from five matches in the Champions League. Despite Yamal’s absence, Barca coach Hansi Flick also chose to rest Raphinha, handing Jesus a rare start up front since his summer move from Arsenal. Khayal Aliyev fired a good early chance straight at Joan Garcia as Sabah threatened in attack, against Barca’s notably fragile defence. Barca midfielder Pedri was denied at the other end before Sabah hit the crossbar, with Ivan Lepinjica’s looping effort beating Garcia but not the woodwork. Gordon broke the deadlock in the 31st minute after Sabah goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov pushed Adeyemi’s cross into his path. The England international netted four goals in his prior appearance in Baku, against Qarabag for Newcastle last season, and was Barca’s brightest player. Gordon had a second effort ruled out for offside against Jesus in the build-up, before the interval. The winger struck six minutes into the second half after Jesus’s effort was saved and the rebound came his way. It was the first of three goals in 10 minutes for the Catalan giants, with Adeyemi notching after Alejandro Balde crossed for him. Jesus bundled home Barca’s fourth of the night from almost on the goalline after Pokatilov parried Jules Kounde’s header. Barcelona had kept a clean sheet against Aston Villa in their previous European clash, after conceding in the previous 18, but were unable to add another. Joy-Lance Mickels pulled one back for Champions League debutants Sabah with a cool finish after Christian Nwachukwu pulled the ball across for him. Adeyemi crashed a shot off the bar as Barcelona threatened sporadically in the final stages without adding to their already ample tally. nigeria.title: Nigeria needs experienced, courageous leaders to tackle challenges, Amaechi hails Atiku at 80
nigeria.description: Former Minister of Transportation, Rotimi Amaechi, has congratulated former Vice President Atiku Abubakar on his 80th birthday, saying Nigeria needs leaders with the experience, courage and capacity to address its economic and security challenges. Amaechi, in a birthday message issued on Wednesday, described Atiku as a distinguished statesman, entrepreneur, philanthropist and patriot whose contributions to Nigeria’s political, economic and social development remained significant. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), turned 80 on Wednesday. Amaechi, a former governor of Rivers State, recalled Atiku’s tenure as Vice President between 1999 and 2007, noting his role in consolidating the Fourth Republic and driving economic reforms. He also highlighted Atiku’s leadership of the National Council on Privatisation, saying his contributions reflected his belief in private-sector development and an enabling business environment. The former minister also commended Atiku’s entrepreneurial investments in agriculture, logistics and real estate, as well as his establishment of the American University of Nigeria, Yola. He said the university reflected Atiku’s commitment to education and human capital development. Amaechi further acknowledged Atiku’s philanthropic activities, particularly his support for educational opportunities for disadvantaged Nigerians and young people affected by the Chibok tragedy. Looking ahead to the 2027 general election, Amaechi said Nigeria required leadership capable of restoring economic confidence, strengthening national security, improving education and healthcare, and ensuring reliable electricity supply. He also backed Atiku’s proposed reintroduction of petroleum production subsidy, arguing that the policy could reduce transportation costs and ease the burden of rising prices on households. According to Amaechi, Nigeria needs a people-centred development agenda that prioritises entrepreneurship, technological innovation, human capital development and private-sector-led growth. He expressed confidence in Atiku’s ambition to contest the 2027 presidential election, saying the country needed leaders who understood its challenges and were prepared to take difficult decisions. Amaechi also called for a Nigeria where young people could find opportunities at home, farmers could prosper, businesses could grow and citizens could access quality education regardless of their backgrounds. He wished Atiku good health, wisdom and strength, while commending his contributions to public service, education, philanthropy and the country’s democratic development. “At 80, your journey is not merely a story of past accomplishments but a reminder that experience must be deployed in the service of the future,” Amaechi said. business.title: Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Committee, Heads to Floor
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Committee, Heads to Floor A bill that would write the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law is now eligible for a vote on the House floor, after the House Financial Services Committee formally reported it on Tuesday. The American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, H.R. 8957, was filed with amendments as House Report 119-894 and placed on the Union Calendar as Calendar No. 789 on Nov. 24, according to congressional records. The committee had voted 28-21 to advance the bill at a Sept. 16 markup. Rep. Nick Begich, an Alaska Republican, introduced the bill on May 21. It now lists 23 cosponsors, including Rep. Jared Golden, a Maine Democrat, with Reps. Byron Donalds and Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida added on Nov. 24. What the amended bill does The reported text directs the Treasury secretary to set up a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a separate Digital Asset Stockpile within 180 days of the law taking effect. Bitcoin owned by the federal government would move into the reserve, while other digital assets would go to the stockpile. The centerpiece is a lock-up. Treasury would have to hold all bitcoin deposited in the reserve for at least 20 years after enactment, and during that period no reserve bitcoin could be “sold, swapped, auctioned, encumbered, or otherwise disposed of for any purpose.” After the 20 years, the Treasury secretary could recommend selling up to 10% of the reserve in any two-year period. Two years before the holding period ends, Treasury would have to send Congress recommendations on whether to keep holding or begin a gradual release. Federal agencies would have 60 days after enactment to give Treasury a full accounting of the bitcoin and other digital assets they hold or have seized. Until the reserve is set up, agencies could not sell those coins except for national security, when required by law or a court, or to return assets to crime victims. The bill also creates a Proof of Reserve system. Treasury would publish an annual report on total holdings, transactions and control of private keys, checked by an independent auditor with expertise in cryptographic attestations, while the Government Accountability Office would provide oversight. States could choose to store their own bitcoin in segregated accounts inside the federal reserve, keeping title to the coins and the right to withdraw them. Changes from Begich’s original version The committee rewrote the bill before reporting it. Begich’s introduced text asked Treasury and Commerce to study funding bitcoin purchases with surplus remittances from Federal Reserve Banks or a revaluation of the Fed’s gold certificates, as well as with tax payments, tariff revenue and gifts. Those options are gone from the amended study, which now looks at swapping other digital assets in the stockpile, forfeitures and settlements, and partnerships with states or private entities. business.title: Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypto Tax Data Sharing Starting in 2028
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypto Tax Data Sharing Starting in 2028 Switzerland’s Federal Council has approved 57 countries and territories with which the country plans to automatically share tax information on crypto users starting in 2028, extending its long-standing bank data exchange to bitcoin and other digital assets. The list includes all European Union member states, the United Kingdom and various G20 countries, the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) said in a release on Wednesday. The exchange will run under the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, known as CARF. With the decision, Switzerland intends to implement the crypto exchange at the same time as other global asset management centers, according to the release. The government did not name the 57 jurisdictions beyond those broad groups, and it did not publish the full list alongside the announcement. Exchanges only with partners that qualify Data will not flow to every name on the list. An exchange will take place only if a partner jurisdiction wants to swap information with Switzerland and meets the conditions of the OECD standard, in particular its requirements on confidentiality and data security. Before any financial account or crypto data changes hands, the Federal Council will run a targeted check of whether each partner complies with OECD standards. It will rely on a review mechanism Parliament approved on Sept. 28, 2026, which covers both the older exchange of bank account data and the new crypto exchange. The domestic legal basis for the crypto exchange took effect on Jan. 1, 2026. Earlier this month, though, the SIF said the framework could not be implemented before Jan. 1, 2027, because the partner list still needed approval and notifications had to go to the OECD. The rules do not apply this year. The Council also approved Armenia and Rwanda as new partners for the exchange of financial account information, with first exchanges due in 2028, and signed off on two notifications needed to carry out the exchange. Both partner lists were broadly supported during public consultations in 2024 and 2025, the government said. Down from 74 partners The final list is shorter than first planned. In June 2025, the Federal Council proposed 74 countries relevant to the crypto market, including all EU states, the UK and most G20 members. That plan left out the United States and Saudi Arabia, and it targeted a 2026 start with first data exchanges in 2027. Wednesday’s release did not say which countries were dropped or whether the U.S. is now on the list. The U.S. has committed to begin CARF exchanges by 2029, according to the OECD’s Global Forum, which lists Switzerland among 27 jurisdictions aiming for first exchanges by 2028. business.title: Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Passports, Bank Accounts and Wallet Addresses
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Passports, Bank Accounts and Wallet Addresses South Korean crypto exchange Bithumb said Wednesday that an October hack of its internal systems exposed more people and far more personal data than it first disclosed, including passport numbers, bank account numbers and crypto wallet addresses. The exchange also said the intruder had access for about 15 days before being shut out, not the roughly one hour it reported last month. In an updated notice posted Nov. 25, Bithumb said a follow-up review of the breach of Daou Office, its internal mobile groupware system, turned up additional affected people and additional types of data. The company said the new findings stem from the same incident it disclosed on Oct. 29. Bithumb breach ran for 15 days Bithumb now says an unauthorized outside party accessed the groupware system from 1:49 p.m. on Oct. 12 to 3:22 p.m. on Oct. 27, Korea time, and took personal information and files stored there. That is a sharp change from its first account. Bithumb had said the hack lasted about an hour, from 11:28 a.m. to 12:27 p.m. on Oct. 27, and that it detected the intrusion at 12:14 p.m. that day. The revised timeline means the attacker went unnoticed for more than two weeks. Bithumb first reported that the data of 6,444 customers and 715 employees, or 7,159 people in total, had been exposed. It did not give an updated count on Wednesday. The notice lists customers, employees of partner companies and current and former staff among those affected. Passports, bank accounts and wallet addresses The list of exposed data now runs to 19 items. It includes member numbers, names, mobile numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, resident registration numbers, passport numbers and driver’s license numbers. It also covers bank account numbers, home addresses, gender, nationality, copies of ID documents, occupations, employer names and work contact details, as well as transaction histories and wallet addresses. Bithumb said not every item applies to every person, and that affected users will be told individually by email and text message what was taken. For crypto users, the wallet addresses and transaction records stand out. Paired with names and phone numbers, that kind of data can help scammers target people they know hold digital assets. Bithumb said Daou Office is an internal business system separate from customer exchange accounts and asset data. It said it has found no sign that its exchange service systems or customer database were directly breached, and that it has stepped up real-time monitoring of unusual trades and withdrawals. Bithumb promises compensation The exchange said it blocked the attacker’s IP addresses, fixed the vulnerability behind the incident and is running a security review of all of its externally exposed services. The department announced the results of an anti-scam surge that followed President Donald Trump’s Executive Order 14390, signed March 6. Since then, prosecutors have acted in more than 400 cases, bringing new charges, extraditions, guilty verdicts and sentences across 85 federal districts. U.S. agents also helped police in more than 10 countries raid foreign scam call centers and compounds that targeted Americans. Thirty defendants were extradited to face charges in U.S. courts. “Predatory scams against the American people will not be tolerated,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said. “The unprecedented results of this surge are just the beginning.” More than $1 billion in crypto frozen Crypto sits at the center of much of the effort. The State Department said the U.S. and Southeast Asian law enforcement it funds and trains have helped freeze more than $1 billion in stolen cryptocurrency and take down more than 1.4 million fraudulent websites and accounts. The Justice Department’s Scam Center Strike Force, formed in 2025 to go after Southeast Asian crypto fraud, says its crypto seizure team has restrained about $1.08 billion in cryptocurrency from these schemes. The team is focused on returning stolen funds to victims. The FBI’s Operation Blackout has restrained nearly $17 billion in illicit funds, seized more than 14,000 digital devices and helped dismantle more than 29 scam compounds across Asia, Africa and the Middle East, the department said. The FBI also helped free and repatriate more than 2,200 trafficked workers forced to run scams inside those compounds. “The message to these scam syndicates is clear: if you target Americans, justice will find you,” FBI Director Kash Patel said. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. sports.description: Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images The Pittsburgh Steelers epitomized organizational dysfunction on Wednesday night. After the team announced late on Tuesday night that veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers wouldn’t be starting Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos and would be inactive instead, Rodgers decided to call into The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday afternoon. During his call, Rodgers asserted that Steelers head coach MikeMcCarthy had completely checked out and was falling asleep and snoring in team meetings and had lost most of the locker room when he ended a rambling speech in the locker room with “One, two, three, Packers!” On a potential return to the organization, Rodgers said “that ship has sailed,” and sure enough, the four-time NFL MVP was released later that day. Despite multiple sports media members and former Steelers saying their sources within the organization had confirmed Rodgers’ claims, one of Rodgers’ former teammates, T.J. Lang, who played with the quarterback with the Green Bay Packers under McCarthy, was disgusted with Rodgers’ tell-all. “I think it’s despicable,” Lang said on 97.1 The Ticket. “I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has bitched about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates, airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media. He has blacklisted, I don’t know how many, former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he was sick of it. Honestly, I don’t even know if I want to watch the whole thing. It’s just unnecessary. “It’s a victim mentality. It’s a poor me, woe is me. Oh, I thought this, and it wasn’t that. And I’m sick, man. I’ve been in a group chat with, with a whole lot of former teammates that feel the exact same way that I do.” Lang went on to say that Rodgers’ behavior was completely unnecessary and that in his eight years playing under McCarthy, he came away loving the coach. TJ Lang on his former teammate Aaron Rodgers https://t.co/0oiS3PybCn — 97.1 The Ticket: (@971theticketxyt) November 25, 2026 “And I talked to Mike McCarthy on Monday night, and, still have a great relationship with him. I haven’t talked to Aaron Rodgers in probably five years. I can’t remember the last time he returned a text. I don’t have a relationship with him. And I think it’s just absolutely despicable what he just did to Big Mike. “Truth or not, truth or not, nobody knows. We’re not in those meetings. We don’t know that. But to air the grievances and to completely try to bury a man that you’ve been a quarterback under for going back to Green Bay, I don’t know, 15, 16 seasons?” It’ll be interesting to see if and how this impacts Rodgers’ legacy. Whatever the case, if this is it for the quarterback, who has been steadfast throughout the season that this would be his final one in the NFL and reportedly doesn’t have a ton of interest at the moment, it’s an ugly end to what’s been a spectacular career. sports.title: Motorcycle rider who took stunning cricket catch found
sports.description: "I told my friend riding the motorcycle to duck his head. I'm going to catch it." These are the words of Mehran Khan, who amazed sports fans around the world when he caught a cricket ball while sitting on the back of a moving motorcycle. Mehran was passing a match in the Swat Premier League in Mingora when a ball sailed out of the ground towards him, with the passenger reaching out to catch it one-handed. Speaking to the BBC, he said of the grab, which has gone viral online: "I didn't think I would actually catch it." The employee of the Public Health Engineering Department was on his way home from work when he saw the ball being struck. "I'm a cricket fan. I play cricket myself and I watch it too. I saw that Abrar Lala was at the crease and then he hit a six," he said. "I told him [the friend who was driving] to duck his head. I'm going to catch it. Then I caught it." "I made the effort, but I didn't expect to catch it. I thought it would fall somewhere nearby, but by the grace of God I managed to catch it." According to Mehran, immediately after the catch the Swat Premier League organisers announced a prize of 10,000 Pakistani rupees (about £27.60) for him, funded by the Pakistan Army. The Marghazar resident was caught by surprise when the recording of the catch spread so quickly online, saying: "The video went viral overnight. I didn't even know about it." He expressed his happiness at receiving the award, saying he was grateful to God, and added that he had returned the ball after taking the catch. "People are saying I was taking the ball away with me, but that's not true. I returned it," he said. Swat Strikers won the match against GKR Dir by 34 runs, and Mehran urged the organisers to continue holding the tournament every year, describing it as an "excellent competition". Mehran Khan is from Marghazar in the Swat region of northern Pakistan [BBC] One of the most unusual catches There have been several remarkable catches by spectators at cricket matches in the past. In 1987, during a match in Australia, a cameraman casually caught one of former England all-rounder Ian Botham's sixes while holding a cigarette in his mouth. In 2014, during a New Zealand domestic match, a spectator slid down a slope and completed a one-handed catch. Last year, in a match between Australia and South Africa, a fan caught a ball with one hand while holding two drink cans in the other. Mehran's one-handed catch while sitting on a moving motorcycle will join them in cricketing history. Get cricket news sent straight to your phone

sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Before Caleb Williams became the Chicago Bears’ quarterback, Thanksgiving football meant a spot on the couch beside his dad. His mom made creamed spinach, they grabbed a bag of Tostitos, and the games became part of the holiday. It’s a familiar scene for football fans: food on the table, family in the room and the television on while the afternoon slips into evening. Williams remembers watching the Dallas Cowboys and another NFC team playing while he and his dad enjoyed the snack. On Thursday, he’ll be on the other side of the screen. Williams and the Bears visit the Detroit Lions in a Thanksgiving game with far more at stake than holiday bragging rights. sports.title: Set point #14: A season in review
sports.description: There’s no denying the fact that there was a lot of bad this season. Northwestern finished the year 8-20 overall and 1-16 in the Big Ten, losing 14 straight games before beating Iowa in the final week. The ‘Cats were swept 10 times during Big Ten play and ranked at the bottom of the conference in most of the major statistical categories, including wins. The season started off with a disappointing loss to a George Mason team that went .500 in its conference slate, and ended with a stretch of 16 losses in 17 games. There’s no other way to put it: the ‘Cats were not a good volleyball team. However, as I’ve spent the majority of the past 13 editions of this column critiquing the lack of competitiveness shown by Northwestern, I’ll try to keep the season finale one of hope. And, don’t get it twisted, there is hope to be had. Maya Stillwell and Hayley Schaaf broke out as a freshman middle duo. Stillwell ended the year with 120 kills and a team-high 82 blocks while hitting .279 in her 100 sets played. Schaaf totaled 86 kills and 35 blocks while hitting a team-high .299. The two steadily improved throughout the year, and Stillwell looked like one of the conference’s better middle blockers at times toward the end of the season. Both Stillwell and Schaaf can improve their blocking rhythm and attacking precision heading into next season, but if both stay with the ‘Cats, they should form a youthful and exciting middle group when combined with sophomore Kayla Kauffman. Setter Ellie Stiernagle was another impressive freshman. Though she had some defensive issues at points throughout the season, she became the staple of Northwestern. Stiernagle started 26 of the 26 matches she appeared in, finishing the year with 910 assists. She also had 16 aces and 46 blocks to go along with 188 digs. At 6-foot-2, Stiernagle is tall enough to play all around, and she proved it throughout the year. Northwestern’s serve receive was a big problem this season, but Stiernagle frequently gave her hitters chances to swing despite less-than-ideal passes. Sophomore libero Lauren Dignan was the major bright spot on the defensive end. She averaged 3.59 digs per set, good for seventh in the Big Ten, totaling 337. Although it was hard to defend with a questionable NU block often allowing clean hits or weird touches, Dignan did the best she could to cover the entire floor. Northwestern had three quality liberos on the roster, including Drew Wright and Gigi Navarrete, but Dignan was the one most trusted in the opposite-colored jersey. If the block can improve and the passing around her is shored up, Dignan could be in for a breakout junior season. The other key pieces of the team that will return next season are the two kill leaders, junior opposite hitter Mara Stiglic and sophomore outside hitter Bella Bullington. I’ve talked a lot about the pitfalls of these two in this column, but it’s unfair to look past the fact that they did their job. Stiglic ended the year with a team-high 323 kills

technology.title: European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment
technology.description: Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory. Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid's 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation. But scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next. "We knew right away that the impact was successful, that DART made a really, really large mess," said Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist at the International Space Science Institute in Bern, Switzerland. "H owever, we didn’t really know what kind of mess. We were still missing pieces of the puzzle." Artist's illustration of the Hera spacecraft with its two deployable CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, in the vicinity of the Didymos binary asteroid system. Credit: ESA-Science Office Following up The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft recently arrived in the vicinity of Didymos and Dimorphos after a two-year journey from a launch pad in Florida . On Wednesday, ESA released Hera's first views of the scar left by DART on Dimorphos . The images show the car-sized impactor carved out a crater the size of a stadium, nearly as big as Dimorphos itself, a rugged chunk of extraterrestrial rock measuring about 500 feet (151 meters) across. Mission planners selected Didymos and Dimorphos for the deflection experiment because they are similar to many near-Earth asteroids, but there's no risk of them striking our home planet. Scientists weren't sure what Hera would find when it got to the double asteroid, currently orbiting the Sun about 120 million miles (193.5 million kilometers) from Earth. " I would say we had two kinds of predictions: either we made a crater, or we reshaped the asteroid," said Patrick Michel, Hera's principal investigator from Côte d’Azur Observatory in Nice, France. "In fact, we did both because the crater is so large that the shape has changed. Therefore, we are in a sort of a transition between just cratering and global transformation, and we are still not sure how this can happen." technology.title: The security of US water systems is even leakier than we thought
technology.description: American water systems are even less secure than we thought, according to a study of 236 technology vendors that provide gear to US drinking water, wastewater, and industrial water systems. The federal government has issued 4,014 security advisories for industrial control systems and cataloged 1,792 vulnerabilities known to have been exploited in cyberattacks. A new index, called Water Supply Chain Watch and published by exposure management firm Securin, however, found almost twice as many vulnerabilities as public records identified – including 20 exploited flaws that weren't even in the federal government's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The security provider compared data on water-tech vendors with records from the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the FBI, and WaterISAC, drawing on CISA advisory data through November 20 and KEV catalog entries through November 23. It found that federal water advisories hit their highest level this year since 2020. However, the volume of security alerts isn't a reliable predictor of real-world attacks, the researchers noted. Five vendors – Rockwell Automation (58), Advantech (48), Schneider Electric (35), Siemens (26), and ABB (24) – account for 191 of the 376 water-tagged security advisories. The No. 2 firm, Advantech, accounted for the highest number of vulnerabilities rated critical, but none of the CVEs in its advisories appear in CISA's KEV catalog. Unitronics, on the other hand, accounted for only two water-tagged security advisories, but at least 75 of its controllers were compromised between November 2023 and January 2024 by attackers taking advantage of default or missing passwords. The report also highlights another disconnect between water-related CVEs and real-world cyberattacks, which don't always require attackers to exploit software bugs. The July intrusions, which security researchers suspect were the work of Iran-linked attackers , targeted more than 100 water systems , with incidents reported across at least 12 states , and involved poorly secured internet-connected controllers . According to Securin, 791 Rockwell MicroLogix 1400 controllers across multiple industries in the US were exposed to the internet as of November 17. Additionally, research by Forescout cited by the security shop found that most exposed Rockwell controllers in the US – seven in 10 – sit on mobile carrier networks, where poorly secured cellular modems can provide an entry point for attackers. technology.title: Huawei and crew tout homegrown EDA tools to overcome China’s fab deficit
technology.description: Chinese telecom and IT giant Huawei boasted about its advancements in domestic electronic design automation (EDA) software this week, which it needs to accelerate the adoption of homegrown chip manufacturing. EDA is an umbrella term for software, hardware, and services essential to the planning, design, and production of modern chips. Today, Cadence Design Systems, Synopsys, and Siemens dominate the industry, but US export controls have restricted Huawei and other blacklisted Chinese businesses' access to their tools. The US blacklisted Huawei back in 2019 over concerns the telecommunications equipment giant could be forced to inject backdoors into its gear. Unable to access top EDA tools, Huawei’s chip division, HiSilicon, was forced to develop its own with the help of Phlexing Technology. This week, Phlexing chairman Qing He detailed the company’s efforts to bring new EDA tools to support Huawei’s so-called Tau Scaling Law design philosophy. “Tau EDA is the domestic EDA tool chain for Tau chips. It comes from a long, close partnership with Huawei,” he said. We discussed the tech earlier this year, but in a nutshell, it involves using advanced packaging, specifically 3D hybrid bonding, to achieve higher transistor density for a given area. The TSMC of China, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), is still years behind Taiwan, South Korea, and the US on process technology. It currently has the ability to mass-produce chips on the equivalent of a 7 nm process. For comparison, TSMC began producing 5 nm-class products in 2020 and commenced mass production of 2 nm-class chips in late 2025. So, Huawei aims to use 3D packaging to close the gap, but for this to happen, it first needs tools capable of designing such chips, and that’s just what Phlexing claims to have done with its GloryBolt and GloryEX platforms. “Traditional EDA has long handled only single processes. Tau EDA needs to integrate and decompose multiple processes,” He said. “Coupling multi-scale, multi-structure, and multi-physics issues called for new analysis tools.” This, He says, culminated in the co-development of a process design kit (PDK) with Huawei beginning in 2024. These technologies have now gone live. The development comes as Huawei looks to bring larger, more capable processors to market. We previously discussed the company’s latest developments around AI accelerators, near packaged optics, networking, and rack systems. Many of these advancements will depend on multi-die chip packages, enabled by EDA tools, like those built by Phlexing. ®

technology.title: Hera probe finds DART left a stadium-sized dent in asteroid Dimorphos
technology.description: The European Space Agency's Hera probe has revealed a stadium-sized crater on Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA struck with its DART spacecraft in 2022. The Double Asteroid Redirection Test was deliberately crashed into the asteroid on September 26, 2022. The original plan called for a European spacecraft – Asteroid Impact Mission (AIM) – to launch first and observe the before and after effects of DART. AIM was canceled, and the Hera mission launched in 2024. DART was a success. Scientists were able to determine that the impact had indeed changed the orbit of Dimorphos. The question was what else had happened to the asteroid. Scientists spotted ejecta and debris following the DART impact, but the close-up observations by Hera have revealed the full extent of the collision. Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at CNRS / Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur, said: "Scientists debated whether Dimorphos had sustained an impact crater, changed its shape or stayed the same. "Much to our surprise the answer turns out to be all three at once! The face struck by DART has been flattened into an impact crater the size of a sports stadium, which extends across the asteroid's entire width." Scientists also noted that the asteroid is now tumbling in its orbit. Hera is surveying the 151-meter-wide Dimorphos and its larger companion, the 730-meter-wide Didymos, from about 25 to 30 km away. It moves around the pair at roughly 12 cm/s, using thruster firings to trace rectangular paths rather than conventional circular orbits. The plan is to approach closer, to about 13 km, to get higher-resolution snaps. A complicating factor is the discovery that hundreds of orbiting boulders surround the asteroids. Michael Kueppers, ESA's Hera mission scientist, said: "The team will have to take account of these objects in the coming weeks as the mission moves in closer." Hera will deploy two CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, in early 2027. The Italian-led Milani will study surface composition and surrounding dust, while the Luxembourg-led Juventas will use radar to probe Dimorphos's interior before attempting a landing. Scientists also want to measure Dimorphos's mass. Combined with the observed change in its orbit, that will help them assess how effectively DART transferred momentum to the asteroid and improve predictions for future deflection attempts. Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli said: "NASA's DART mission demonstrated that we can change an asteroid's orbit. Hera is now revealing what happened to the asteroid itself. By combining these two missions, humanity is taking a decisive step towards making asteroid deflection a reliable tool for protecting our planet." ®

science.title: December full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Cold Moon
science.description: null The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon).. According to the late, great astronomer Fred Espenak , the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026! When to see the December full moon The full Cold Supermoon will make for a spectacular sight when it rises over the eastern horizon at sunset on Dec. 23, mere hours before reaching maximum illumination. Remember to use Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location. Earth's satellite may appear larger than normal while close to the horizon. This is partly because it is near perigee, when it appears subtly larger in the night sky, but also because of a phenomenon called the moon illusion, which tricks us into perceiving the moon to be bigger than it actually is while in the presence of foreground objects. A yellow full moon rises over Italy. (Image credit: Photo by Lorenzo Di Cola/NurPhoto via Getty Images) The moon may also adopt a striking golden or orange hue around moonrise and moonset. When the moon is low on the horizon, its light travels through more of Earth's atmopshere, scattering shorter, bluer wavelengths of light and allowing longer, redder wavelengths to reach our eyes. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
science.description: null On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights. The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet. NASA's M2-F3 lifting body drops from its carrier plane during a test flight in 1970. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered In the late 1960s and early 1970s, NASA was investigating lifting bodies as an approach to both new aircraft and what future spacecraft, and as its number suggests, the M2-F3 was not the first of its kind. In fact, the M2-F3 was a rebuilt version of its predecessor, the M2-F2 lifting body , after that vehicle crashed in a dry lake bed in California's Mojave Desert during an unpowered test flight. That crash (which appears in the opening of the TV show "The Six-Million-Dollar Man") led to upgrades for a better handling lifting body, NASA said. "When the M2-F2 was rebuilt and redesignated the M2-F3, it was modified with an additional third vertical fin – centered between the tip fins – to improve control characteristics," NASA wrote in an overview . Unpowered glide flights for the M2-F3 began in June 1970, but Dana's flight on Nov. 25 of that year was the first time the vehicle fired up its rocket engine to test its controls under powered flight. One vital upgrade on the vehicle was a set of reaction control thrusters to help maintain its orientation. "A reaction jet control system, similar to thrusters used on orbiting spacecraft, was also installed on the M2-F3 to obtain research data about their effectiveness for vehicle control," NASA wrote . "As the M2-F3’s portion of the lifting body program neared an end, it evaluated a rate command augmentation control system and a side-arm control stick similar to side-arm controllers now used on many modern aircraft." If you want, you can see the M2-F3 vehicle today. NASA donated it to the Smithsonian Institution. It is now hanging at the National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: NASA Enhances Supplier Program, Announces Mentor-Protégé Agreement
science.description: NASA’s Office of Small Business Programs (OSBP) hosted a ceremonial Mentor-Protégé Agreement signing between The Boeing Company and GRACE Aerospace on Oct. 29, 2026, at the U.S. Space and Rocket Center in Huntsville, Alabama. As part of the program, NASA announced its latest Mentor-Protégé Agreement, this one signed between The Boeing Company and GRACE Aerospace. NASA is streamlining the application process for the Small Business Supplier Development Program, as well as reducing administrative requirements, accelerating review and approval timelines, and enhancing incentives for prime contractor participation. These improvements are aimed at making supplier development more accessible, efficient, and closely aligned with NASA’s mission needs. “We have intentionally redesigned the program as a mission-focused tool for strengthening industrial base readiness and mission success,” said Dwight Deneal, assistant administrator, Office of Small Business Programs, NASA Headquarters in Washington. “By simplifying participation and focusing developmental assistance on the capabilities NASA needs most, we are helping build a stronger, more resilient supplier base that can support the agency’s highest-priority missions.” Under the new Mentor-Protégé Agreement, Boeing will provide structured assistance to help GRACE expand its capabilities as a supplier of mission-critical aerospace hardware. Boeing will fund the agreement, valued at nearly $500,000. “Boeing is proud to continue its longstanding relationship with NASA in support of its mission and the opportunities this agreement creates for Boeing, GRACE, and the broader aerospace industrial base,” said Christian Diamond, Mentor-Protégé Program manager and small business liaison officer for Boeing. “Through this partnership, Boeing looks forward to sharing our expertise to support the continued growth and long-term success of a small business while strengthening our supplier base.”

Many large vessels are now legally required to carry automatic identification systems broadcasting their identity and location at regular intervals. Although this has allowed interactions between animals and fisheries to be studied at scale, there are enormous gaps in coverage. In fact, recent research suggests that three-quarters of industrial fishing vessels don’t use the technology, says Jonathan Rutter at the University of Oxford. This is partly because regulations on the types of vessels that are required to share data vary by country. Large satellite ‘blind spots’ also contribute to the problem, he says, and so does subterfuge for the purpose of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing (IUU). The team analysed audio collected from devices attached to seven northern gannets ( Morus bassanus ) and found that one third of the audio detections couldn’t be matched with vessel tracking data – mostly off the UK coast. science.title: SpaceX Starship debris becomes art in Ashley Zelinskie's 'The Weight of Space' (video, photos)
science.description: null When a SpaceX Starship broke apart over Turks and Caicos in Jan. 2025, pieces of its heat shield washed ashore. Some of that material now hangs on a gallery wall in New York City, embedded in artist Ashley Zelinskie's print of the very explosion it survived. Look closely at the print and you can see little flakes on the surface. Some of Zelinskie's friends vacationing on the islands had come across pieces of heat-shield tile. "I think you might want these," Zelinskie recalled one friend telling her. She did. The Brooklyn-based artist ground the fragments into dust and worked them into the print. Ashley Zelinskie incorporated dust from recovered SpaceX Starship heat-shield tiles into this print of the vehicle breaking apart over Turks and Caicos. (Image credit: Ashley Zelinskie) The Starship print is part of "Ejecta," which captures rocket plumes and explosions on paper. It's one of four series in Zelinskie's solo exhibition, "The Weight of Space," which opened Nov. 20 at Heft Gallery in Manhattan. Her marble sculptures in "Monuments" depict the Hubble Space Telescope, retired NASA astronaut Mike Massimino's spaceflight gear and more. Five "Launch Sequence" sculptures follow a rocket through liftoff, and the interactive "Crowded Sky" lets visitors track what's currently orbiting overhead in real time. Zelinskie gave Space.com Editor-in-Chief Tariq Malik and me a tour before the gallery doors opened. Massimino joined her that evening to celebrate the exhibition and their collaboration on "Monuments." You can watch the tour in the video above. Monuments Massimino turned up in our first look at Zelinskie's work, too. In 2022, I photographed the two of them beside her "Exploration JWST" sculpture at "Unfolding the Universe: First Light," an exhibit inspired by the James Webb Space Telescope's first images. Four years later, Massimino stood in a New York gallery looking at another Zelinskie sculpture. "That's my arm there," he told Malik.
